title: Countable compact exhaustion: swapping 'for all compact K ⊆ U' with 'for a.e. t'
statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, and (F_t)_{t∈ℝ} a family of set functions F_t : 𝒫(ℝ^P) → [0, ∞], each monotone (A ⊆ B ⇒ F_t(A) ≤ F_t(B)). Assume that for every compact K ⊆ U, F_t(K) ≠ ∞ for Lebesgue-a.e. t ∈ ℝ. Then for Lebesgue-a.e. t ∈ ℝ: F_t(K) ≠ ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U.
lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (F : ℝ → Set (Euclid P) → ℝ≥0∞), IsOpen U → (∀ t, Monotone (F t)) → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∀ᵐ t, F t K ≠ ∞) → ∀ᵐ t, ∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → F t K ≠ ∞
